The filter is a unity-gain Sallen-Key lowpass, so the -3 dB frequency is set by the passives:

fc = 1/(2π√(R1·R2·C1·C2)) ≈ 62 MHz from the netlist values, versus the simulated 21 MHz and a target of about 190 MHz.

The measured fc is about 3x too low, so the R·C product is roughly 9–10x too large. A single resistor scaled up by about 10x fits this best: R1 = 29.9 kΩ (or R2 = 11.3 kΩ) would be about 2.99 kΩ (or 1.13 kΩ) in the intended design, which would put fc near 190–200 MHz. The DC gain (0.018 dB) and near-zero peaking are consistent with a correct unity-gain buffer and a low-Q passive network, so the op amp is less likely to be the fault. C1 looks like a deliberate round value (100 fF), which makes it less likely to be the corrupted element. R1 ranks first because its value is the largest in the RC product.
